svg.title: Options for listening to Dataverse events, as a ladder
svg.desc: A ladder of questions, asked from top to bottom; the first yes decides. One: must the listener stop or change the operation? Then a synchronous plug-in step inside the pipeline. Two: is the need a copy of tables for analytics? Then a managed link to Azure Synapse or Fabric, not events. Three: does the consumer keep its own copy and tolerate a delay of fifteen minutes or more? Then the consumer pulls with change tracking. Four: is it a time-ordered stream that readers analyse or replay, or more than a million events a day? Then Azure Event Hubs. Five: must nothing be lost while the listener is down, are there several subscribers, or must events of one key stay in order? Then Azure Service Bus, a topic for several subscribers and a queue for one. Six: do makers own the reaction and is the volume modest? Then a cloud flow with a Dataverse or business event trigger. Otherwise: a webhook, an HTTPS POST of the execution context to one endpoint. On the right, facts for each rung: plug-in, two-minute limit, in the transaction; managed link, no code; change tracking, includes deletions, the consumer owns the token; Event Hubs, partitions, consumer groups, retention, no per-event delete; Service Bus, asynchronous steps only, payload limit 192 kilobytes, retried by the asynchronous service; cloud flow, connectors and run history; webhook, synchronous or asynchronous steps, 60-second time-out, payload limit 256 kilobytes, one more attempt only for 502, 503 and 504.
svg.text: Something happened in Dataverse. Who needs to know, and how sure must it be?
Ask from the top. The first "yes" decides.

g.text: 1. Must it stop or change the operation?
a rule that has to hold for every caller,
never call an outside system from it
2. Is it a copy of tables for analytics?
reports over history, joined with other data
3. Does the consumer keep its own copy
and tolerate 15 minutes or more of delay?
new, changed and deleted rows since
a token; the consumer owns the pace
4. Is it a stream to analyse or replay,
or more than a million events a day?
readers keep a position; no dead-letter
5. Must nothing be lost while the listener
is down? Several subscribers? Order per key?
each event matters and gets handled once
row trigger or "When an action is
one HTTP consumer that answers quickly
